## Web Searcher: vendor-official-guidance

Research question: "State of the art (as of July 2026) in AI coding-agent governance and harness design — the problem space of the claude.md-workflow repo: project instruction files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md-style), lifecycle hooks, deterministic verification gates, persistent agent memory/working-state across sessions and compaction, behavioral guardrails against scope creep/overclaiming/sycophancy, git-level enforcement, task contracts, and parallel multi-agent orchestration (worktree isolation, orchestrator/reduce patterns, adversarial review). Survey and compare best practices from: Anthropic (Claude Code, Agent SDK, skills/hooks/subagents), OpenAI (Codex, AGENTS.md), Google (Gemini CLI/Jules/Antigravity), Microsoft (GitHub Copilot agents, AutoGen/agent frameworks), NVIDIA (agent toolkits/NeMo), xAI (Grok agents/coding); and non-Western labs: Moonshot AI (Kimi K2.5 agentic training), Zhipu/Z.ai (GLM-5.x coding agents), DeepSeek (agentic/tool-use practices), Tencent (recent Hunyuan model launch and agent tooling), MiniMax (M-series agentic models), Alibaba Qwen if relevant; plus respected independents: Nous Research (Hermes 4/Hermes agent), Fundamental Research Labs (Peter Wang co-founder), the team behind the Ornith-1.0 LLM, tinygrad/George Hotz's approach to minimal harnesses, and any other influential open agent-harness projects (e.g. OpenHands, SWE-agent, Aider, Cline, Devin/Cognition). For each: what they prescribe for instruction-file structure and length, memory persistence, verification/eval gating, multi-agent patterns, and prompt-vs-deterministic enforcement. Identify convergent consensus, notable divergences (especially Western vs Chinese lab practices), and concrete, citable insights that should shape a 2026 rewrite of a drop-in governance kit for coding agents. Note if any named entity cannot be verified to exist (e.g. 'Ornith-1.0') rather than guessing."

Your angle: **vendor-official-guidance** — Primary sources: what Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google officially prescribe for project instruction files, lifecycle hooks, and memory — the backbone of any governance kit comparison.
Search query: `CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md best practices 2026 instruction file length structure Anthropic Claude Code hooks OpenAI Codex Gemini CLI GEMINI.md official documentation`

## Task
Use WebSearch with the query above (or a refined version). Return the top 4-6 most relevant results.
Rank by relevance to the ORIGINAL question, not just the search query. Skip obvious SEO spam/content farms.
Include a short snippet capturing why each result is relevant.

Structured output only.

Based on the web search results, here's comprehensive information about CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, best practices, and instruction file structure for Anthropic Claude Code and other AI coding assistants in 2026:

## Core Instruction Files by Tool

Every major AI coding tool now reads a configuration file from your project: Claude Code looks for CLAUDE.md, Codex CLI reads AGENTS.md, Gemini CLI checks for GEMINI.md, GitHub Copilot uses copilot-instructions.md, and Windsurf has .windsurfrules.

## CLAUDE.md Best Practices

**Context Window Management**

Your CLAUDE.md file should contain as few instructions as possible - ideally only ones which are universally applicable to your task. Research suggests frontier LLMs can reliably follow around 150-200 instructions, and Claude Code's system prompt already uses about 50 of those, so keep your CLAUDE.md concise — ideally under 300 lines.

**Optimal Structure**

A good structure, top to bottom includes: one-line project description, tech stack (framework, language, versions, database), commands (build, test, lint, run, deploy with exact invocations), architecture (the 3–5 directories that matter), conventions (patterns the team enforces), boundaries (what's off-limits), and pointers to agent_docs/.

**What NOT to Include**

One of the most common mistakes is including code style guidelines. Never send an LLM to do a linter's job — LLMs are comparably expensive and incredibly slow compared to traditional linters and formatters. Code style guidelines add instructions and mostly-irrelevant code snippets into your context window, degrading performance.

## AGENTS.md File Structure

AGENTS.md is used for universal instructions that work with Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code. If your team uses multiple AI tools, you can maintain a single AGENTS.md and it will work with Claude Code automatically.

## Hooks and Extensions

Claude Code supports cross-platform sound notification system through hooks, with hook events configured including PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Notification, Stop, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreCompact, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Setup, PermissionRequest, TeammateIdle, TaskCompleted, and ConfigChange.

## Subagents and Advanced Features

A subagent does not receive the full Claude Code system prompt — it only gets its system prompt (plus basic environment details like working directory). That's a big part of why they stay "clean" and focused.

## File Discovery Hierarchy

Claude Code also reads AGENTS.md as a fallback if no CLAUDE.md is found in a directory. You can also place a CLAUDE.md inside .claude/ at the project root for settings you want separated from the canonical top-level file — Claude Code will load .claude/CLAUDE.md alongside the root one.

Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about AGENTS.md, OpenAI Codex, and related CLI tools:

## AGENTS.md Overview

AGENTS.md is a simple, open format for guiding coding agents, functioning as a README for agents. AGENTS.md is a plain Markdown file that tells AI coding agents how your project works.

Originally popularized by OpenAI's Codex CLI, the format has since been adopted as an open standard by the Agentic AI Foundation (a directed fund under the Linux Foundation) and is now supported across Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and dozens of other tools.

## OpenAI Codex's AGENTS.md Guide

Codex reads AGENTS.md files before doing any work, and by layering global guidance with project-specific overrides, you can start each task with consistent expectations, no matter which repository you open.

### Discovery Hierarchy

In your Codex home directory (defaults to ~/.codex, unless you set CODEX_HOME), Codex reads AGENTS.override.md if it exists. Otherwise, Codex reads AGENTS.md, using only the first non-empty file at this level.

Starting at the project root (typically the Git root), Codex walks down to your current working directory. If Codex cannot find a project root, it only checks the current directory. In each directory along the path, it checks for AGENTS.override.md, then AGENTS.md, then any fallback names in project_doc_fallback_filenames.

## Gemini CLI and GEMINI.md

Gemini CLI checks for GEMINI.md. The format has been adopted by the Agentic AI Foundation and is now supported across Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and dozens of other tools.

## Memory and Official Documentation

For Codex specifically, the file is concatenated directly into the context window at the start of every session, meaning whatever you put in AGENTS.md is the first thing Codex reads before it sees any of your prompts.

Recent Codex CLI versions (April 2026 onward) accept a --print-instructions flag that dumps the merged AGENTS.md content it loaded for the current session.

The official AGENTS.md specification is now maintained by the Agentic AI Foundation, making it a cross-vendor standard rather than a tool-specific convention.

## Overview of Claude Code & Agent SDK Architecture

Anthropic documents Claude Code as an agentic coding tool, and exposes the same tool loop programmatically through the Agent SDK. Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with development tools across the terminal, IDEs, desktop, and web.

## Key Architectural Concepts

The strongest behaviors in Claude Code are not prompt-only behaviors—they are architectural behaviors. A hook can deny or defer an action, a sandbox can block a subprocess at the OS level, and an MCP server can add an entire new capability surface—those are system properties, not prompt decorations.

## Hooks System

SDK hooks use callback functions to validate, log, block, or transform agent behavior with available hooks including PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, and UserPromptSubmit. Agent hooks can explore the codebase before making a decision and support async: true to run hooks in the background without blocking Claude's execution.

## Memory and Context Management

Claude's memory tool is a client-side storage-driven persistent memory capability that enables cross-session information retention with context editing showing 84% token savings on long-running tasks. The most important pattern for API agents running across many sessions is the initializer + coding agent pattern.

## Best Practices

Claude Code best practices is the discipline of orchestrating Claude through Commands, Agents, Skills, Hooks, MCP servers, and Memory—keeping each context small, each role focused, and the human in the review seat. Start with skills as they are the easiest to create and provide immediate value, add hooks when you need deterministic enforcement, and use subagents when parallel work or context isolation matters.

I've found comprehensive information about Gemini CLI's GEMINI.md context files and memory system. Here's what the official documentation reveals:

## Overview

Context files, which use the default name GEMINI.md, are a powerful feature for providing instructional context to the Gemini model. You can use these files to give project-specific instructions, define a persona, or provide coding style guides to make the AI's responses more accurate and tailored to your needs.

## Hierarchical Context System

The CLI uses a hierarchical system to source context. It loads various context files from several locations, concatenates the contents of all found files, and sends them to the model with every prompt.

The hierarchy includes:
- ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md (in your user home directory) - Provides default instructions for all your projects.
- The CLI searches for GEMINI.md files in your configured workspace directories and their parent directories.

## Memory Commands

/memory show: Displays the full, concatenated content of the current hierarchical memory. This lets you inspect the exact instructional context being provided to the model.

/memory reload: Forces a re-scan and reload of all GEMINI.md files from all configured locations.

## Modular Context Files

You can break down large GEMINI.md files into smaller, more manageable components by importing content from other files using the @file.md syntax. This feature supports both relative and absolute paths.

## Memory Storage and Persistence

The agent routes memories to the appropriate Markdown file: shared project instructions go in repository GEMINI.md files, private project notes go in the per-project private memory folder, and cross-project personal preferences go in the global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md file.

The stored facts are automatically included in the hierarchical context system for all future sessions.
